text:
IncidentBot: paging: kv-cache eviction-rate spike + continuous-batching latency cliff on prod-east :rotating_light:

IncidentBot: alert_id=kv_eviction_spike_1956007890, severity=high, affected_service=runtime-serving, hint=rapid KV pageouts correlated with continuous batching ramp.

Marie: acked — I'm oncall. seeing 5xx increase on /v1/generate and token latency jumps to 1.2s p95. placing channel for live mitigation.

Dave: on it, pulling metrics now. can you scope customer impact? any tenant hot tails?

Marie: top-3 tenants by qps: acme-inc, readly, finpix - acme showing highest error spike.

Linh: past hour eviction_rate by shard (prod-east):
```
evictions/sec: [shard-1: 12.4, shard-2: 3.1, shard-3: 0.9, shard-4: 47.2]
kv-cache-size: [shard-4: 11GB (thrashing)]
continuous-batch-window: 64ms -> observed burst to 256ms causing more KV churn
```

Maya: looks like batch-window heuristics combined with a skewed request mix; small requests causing repeated cache misses and full page handoffs.

Marie: quick mitigation options: 1) flip continuous-batching off globally (dangerous for perf/cost) 2) per-customer override to opt out of continuous-batching for top tenants 3) reduce batch-window on shard-4 only 4) throttle or route acme to fallback model. preferences?

Dave: prefer per-customer override + shard-level tweak. global flip will harm latency for many and costly.

sre-lead: +1 to per-customer override. we can apply a scoped flag quickly. prepare rollout steps and canary to 2 nodes first.

Marie: creating feature flag change: 
```
# apply per-customer override for continuous-batching
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  https://console.prod.redwood/api/flags/continuous_batching/overrides \
  -d '{"tenants": ["acme-inc","readly"], "value": false, "scope": "tenant"}'
```

Marie: plan: 1) canary override to acme-inc only on 2 nodes in prod-east (10% of acme traffic), 2) monitor eviction_rate/latency for 5m, 3) if stable, expand to remaining acme nodes, 4) add readly to override if similar pattern, 5) follow with shard-4 batch-window reduction if still noisy.

Dave: will run canary now. hooking up Datadog dashboard and traces. tagging traces with flag=per-cust-canary.

ops-bot: deploy action queued: flag-change-request by Marie (runbook: per-cust-canary-1956007890). ETA start=1956007950.

Marie: executing step 1 (canary).

Dave: canary applied to set [node-aws-prod-east-47, node-aws-prod-east-52] for tenant acme-inc.

Linh: within 90s eviction_rate on shard-4 dropped from 47.2 -> 9.3, p95 latency improved from 1.2s -> 0.45s for canaried nodes.

Maya: good signal. small increase in per-token cost for those requests due to local routing but acceptable.

Marie: expanding override to all acme nodes now.

ops-bot: flag-change applied to tenant acme-inc (all nodes).

Dave: acme errors down to baseline. overall 5xx volume down 78% vs peak.

Marie: next: schedule readly override? readly is lower QPS but shows same pattern. propose apply same override and meanwhile reduce batch-window on shard-4 from 64ms -> 32ms as precaution.

sre-lead: proceed. keep staged rollout for readly (canary then full). for shard tweak, update kernel config with a 5-min canary then global.

Marie: readly canary in 2m. tagging incident with customer-impact label and CC-ing account-sre.

Maya: quick note — we should not forget to add an autoscaling rule to avoid sudden node thrash if we see reprise after flag removal. filing short task: AUTO-3956.

Dave: readly canary applied. metrics look similar, no regressions. expanding.

ops-bot: shard config change queued: reduce batch-window shard-4 -> 32ms, runbook ID shard-batch-window-1956007890. scheduled start=1956008030.

Linh: after shard change p95 latency across prod-east stabilized at 0.38s and eviction rates normalized.

Marie: marking incident mitigated. will keep this channel open for 1h for monitoring.

sre-lead: assign postmortem to Marie + Linh + Maya. timeline and customer impact (acme, readly, finpix). severity=SEV2.

Marie: noted. adding preliminary notes to the incident tracker and tagging legal for potential customer escalation.

Dave: handing off to next oncall: @Linh, I'm done for my rotation. leaving action items in the thread.

Linh: taking handoff. I'll watch the dashboards and prepare the postmortem draft. :thumbsup:

IncidentBot: incident mitigated at 1956008095, incident_id=kv_eviction_spike_1956007890.

Marie: thanks everyone. great quick collaboration.
